At its base, raw data (noise) undergoes transformation into structured evidence using domain-specific filters and models. This evidence then feeds into a signal extraction mechanism that identifies actionable patterns—this is the 'signal room'. From there, these signals inform high-level decisions (judgments), which are evaluated against historical outcomes to refine future predictions. The system's integrity depends on maintaining trust gates: honest empty states, accurate win-rate estimation, and organic value extraction from the 163 library map rather than rigid task lists. Failure occurs when noise overwhelms signal or when assumptions about data validity are violated.
